sections.summary: Replaced the pathspec-filtered `git ls-files --others --ignored` walk with a two-phase listing in a new module: phase 1 asks git only for collapsed ignored directories (`--directory --no-empty-directory`), phase 2 drops entries under EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_SET and expands the survivors with an async recursive readdir that stops at nested-repository boundaries (emitting `<dir>/`), skips `.git` and excluded directory names, filters `.pyc/.pyd/.pyo`, and is bounded by depth 12, 32 expanded directories and MAX_CACHED_PATHS. The listing was also taken off the refresh critical path: it is raced against a 400 ms deadline, a miss reuses the last successful set and merges the fresh one into the published snapshot when it lands (guarded so it only ever folds into the snapshot the refresh itself produced), announced through a new `setSnapshotObserver` hook that the session registry publishes. `GIT_IGNORED_EXCLUSION_PATHSPECS` was deleted and the EXCLUDED_* constants moved into the new module so both the listing and the ripgrep exclusions share one definition. Measured `RepositoryService.refresh()` on ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3: 45-53 ms for 3,026 paths, against the 3,520 ms baseline, with the same path count as the old command.

sections.deviations: The `#visiblePaths` cache keys the ignored side on the expanded list (array identity first, then element-wise) rather than on the phase-1 buffer; the expanded list subsumes the buffer, and the phase-1 buffer alone is not a safe key because files inside an unchanged ignored directory do change. The service-level late merge is covered through the extracted, deterministic `withIgnoredListingDeadline` helper rather than by slowing a real git child inside RepositoryService, which has no injection seam.

sections.summary: Every git/gh/rg child now spawns with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, added as a shared `commandEnvironment()` in gitCommands.ts and applied to both `runCommand`'s execFile options and `GitObjectReader`'s `git cat-file --batch` spawn — equivalent to `--no-optional-locks` on every subcommand including the ones gh runs. Verified directly on a temp repo that a plain `git status --porcelain=v2` moves `.git/index` mtime while the same command with the variable set does not. As belt and braces, `refresh()` announces `.git/index` through the existing `#selfWriteObserver` before the git commands and again once they settle, so the 1 s self-write window covers the event however long the commands took. `normalizeChangedPath` still admits `.git/index`, so a `git commit` from a terminal (which also moves HEAD and refs) still refreshes.

sections.summary: `refresh()` is now a dedupe wrapper around the renamed private `#refreshSnapshot()`. Callers that want the state a run is already fetching get that run's promise; a caller that asks after a write to the tree or index gets a fresh run chained behind the current one instead of racing it, and the queued run re-reads the mutation counter when it actually starts so callers arriving while it waits need no cycle of their own. `#mutation` is bumped by `switchBranch`, `pullCurrentBranch`, `checkoutPullRequest` and `saveWorkingFile`; `dispose()` clears the in-flight run and both counters. While re-measuring I found that releasing the in-flight slot in a `.finally` chained after the run left it visible two microtask hops past the caller's own `await`, so `await refresh(); refresh()` handed back the settled run (a 0 ms second cycle); the release now happens inside the run's own then-handlers, guarded by a `#refreshGeneration` counter.

sections.summary: `repositorySessions.open()` now races the live refresh against a 150 ms deadline through a new `#raceLiveSnapshot`. When the refresh wins, the caller gets the real snapshot (branch, HEAD, statuses, full path list), the watcher is synced with it and nothing redundant is published; when it loses, the caller gets the directory listing and the refresh is published as a change event when it lands, through an extracted `#publishRefreshed` that `#refreshAndPublish` also uses. The race is applied to the new-session branch, the `known != null && current == null` branch and the realpath-collision branch, and a new session's watcher now starts with whichever snapshot was returned. `listRootSnapshot` was rebuilt as a bounded walk: depth 3, cap 2,000 (was depth 2, cap 400), files of each level before its subdirectories so a truncated listing is the top of the tree, dot-entries included, and the skip set is now EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_SET plus `.git` and `vendor`. Measured on core-3: 266 paths (was 84) in 1.0-2.7 ms warm.

blockers: needs-owner, src/shared/contracts.ts (Track D): P04 has no snapshot discriminator. Wanted edit — add an optional stage field to `RepositorySnapshot`: `/** 'skeleton' is the bounded directory listing shown while git answers. */ stage?: 'skeleton' | 'live'`. With it, `listRootSnapshot` would set `stage: 'skeleton'` and `RepositoryService.#refreshSnapshot` / `#refreshFolder` would set `stage: 'live'`, which is what P27 needs to re-derive the workspace view when a skeleton is replaced. Until then the only signal a renderer has is `kind === 'git' && branch == null && statuses.length === 0`, which is indistinguishable from a folder-kind snapshot.
reviewNotes: Look at these first. (1) `RepositoryService.refresh()` in src/main/repository.ts — the in-flight slot is released inside the run's own then-handlers, guarded by `#refreshGeneration`, deliberately not in a chained `.finally`. My first version used `.finally` and it made `await refresh(); refresh()` return the already-settled run (measured as a bogus 0 ms cycle on core-3); the strengthened test in repository.test.ts pins this. (2) `#mergeIgnoredPaths` only fires when `snapshot.paths === trackedPathsCache.paths`, which is what keeps a late ignored set from being merged onto a snapshot it did not come from (a hydrate, or a newer refresh). Worth a second pair of eyes on that guard. (3) `repositorySessions.open()` now awaits up to 150 ms before returning, and when the race wins it publishes nothing — a behaviour change for the two `current == null` branches, which used to always publish. The reasoning is that the caller receives the snapshot over IPC, but if anything else depended on that publish it would be silent. (4) `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` is set on every `runCommand` child, so it also reaches `gh` and `rg`; intentional (gh shells out to git), harmless for rg. (5) `listRootSnapshot` now returns dotfiles, which changed an existing repository.test.ts assertion — see the P04 deviation note; if the product genuinely wants dotfiles hidden in the open skeleton, that has to change in the live snapshot too, not just the listing. (6) I could not verify the plan's probe targets (`restoreSettled`, open-folder-probe, git-spawn counts) because this track must not build, install or launch the app; the numbers I do have are direct measurements of `RepositoryService.refresh()` (45-53 ms on core-3 for 3,026 paths, down from 3,520 ms) and `listRootSnapshot` (1.0-2.7 ms warm) from throwaway bun scripts in the scratchpad. (7) `EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES` / `EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_SET` / `EXCLUDED_IGNORED_EXTENSIONS` moved from repository.ts to the new src/main/ignoredListing.ts and are imported back; workspaceListing.ts now also imports the directory set. That is a wider blast radius than a pure addition, but it was needed to let the equivalence test rebuild the legacy pathspecs without a circular import. (8) src/main/repositoryWatcher.ts shows a one-line diff against HEAD (`.horus` added to EXCLUDED_SEGMENTS) — that is pre-existing uncommitted work, not mine; I only touched its test.
